slides.title: When Pythagoras is not enough
slides.prompt: Pythagoras needs two known sides and only ever finds a third side. The moment an angle enters the question, sin, cos and tan take over. By the end of this lesson you will have banked 15 marks of real exam working, including a question from an actual past paper.

chapter 1 of 5
Naming the sides

Every trig question starts by naming the three sides relative to the marked angle.

Swap opposite and adjacent and both marks are gone before the calculator even opens. The hypotenuse never changes; the other two names depend on which angle is marked.

slides.title: Three sides, three names
slides.prompt: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, as always. The other two names come from the marked angle $\theta$: the side across from $\theta$ is the opposite, and the side touching $\theta$ is the adjacent.

interaction.hint: Start with the hypotenuse, the side opposite the right angle. Then ask which of the other two touches $\theta$.

config.prompt: Drag each name onto its side. The angle $\theta$ is at the bottom right.

config.successText: Side 1 touches $\theta$, so it is the adjacent. Side 2 is across from $\theta$, so it is the opposite. Side 3 faces the right angle, the hypotenuse.

interaction.hint: Opposite means across from the marked angle, wherever that angle sits.

config.prompt: Now $\theta$ is at the top. Which side is the opposite?

options.whyWrong: Side 2 runs into $\theta$ now, so it has become the adjacent.
The slanted side faces the right angle, so it stays the hypotenuse no matter where $\theta$ sits.

config.successText: Move the angle and the names move with it: side 1 is now across from $\theta$, so it is the opposite. Naming the sides is always the first thing to do, every question.

visual.content:
chapter 2 of 5
The three ratios

Sin, cos and tan are fixed ratios between pairs of sides, decided entirely by the angle.

SOH CAH TOA: sin is opposite over hypotenuse, cos is adjacent over hypotenuse, tan is opposite over adjacent. Writing the right one with the numbers in is the method mark in every question.

slides.title: The ratios belong to the angle
slides.prompt: Drag the angle and watch all three ratios change. Then resize the triangle without touching the angle: the sides grow, but every ratio holds still. That is why one angle is enough to fix the shape of a right-angled triangle.

slides.title: Pick the ratio that connects them

interaction.hint: Name the two sides you have first: one faces $\theta$, one faces the right angle.

config.prompt: You know the side opposite $\theta$ and the hypotenuse. Which ratio connects them?
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='93.8,259 386.3,259 93.8,49' fill='rgba(240,238,234,0.05)' stroke='#c8c6be' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><path d='M 106.8 259 L 106.8 246 L 93.8 246' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><path d='M 386.3 259 L 362.3 259 L 362.3 257.8 L 362.4 256.5 L 362.5 255.3 L 362.8 254.1 L 363.1 252.8 L 363.4 251.6 L 363.8 250.5 L 364.3 249.3 L 364.8 248.2 L 365.4 247.1 L 366.1 246 L 366.8 245 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='352.3' y='247' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>θ</text><text x='77.8' y='154' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff822c' text-anchor='end' dominant-baseline='middle'>7 cm</text><text x='254' y='134.5' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff4670' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>12 cm</text></svg>

options.whyWrong: Cos uses the adjacent, the side touching $\theta$. The $7$ cm side is across from $\theta$.
Tan is opposite over adjacent, and the $12$ cm side is the hypotenuse, not the adjacent.

config.successText: Opposite and hypotenuse is the S of SOH CAH TOA: $\sin\theta = \dfrac{7}{12}$. Naming the sides chose the ratio for you.

interaction.hint: Both known sides touch the right angle.

config.prompt: One from the last topic. Which equation finds this hypotenuse?

options.whyWrong: Both known sides are legs, so their squares are added. Subtraction is for when the hypotenuse is known.
No angle value is given here, and both sides are known. This is a Pythagoras job, not a trig one.

config.successText: Two known sides and no angle is Pythagoras territory: $c = 10$. Trig takes over when an angle joins the question.

visual.content:
chapter 3 of 5
Finding a side

One angle and one side are known. Pick the ratio that links them to the side you want.

Worth 2 marks: one for the ratio with the numbers in, one for the value. Check your calculator says degrees before anything else.

interaction.hint: The hypotenuse faces the right angle, and the right angle is the biggest angle in the triangle.

config.prompt: The hypotenuse is $12$ and the angle is $35°$. Before any working, how long can the opposite side $x$ be?

options.whyWrong: Nothing beats the hypotenuse: it faces the largest angle, so every other side is shorter.
Only the hypotenuse is $12$. If another side matched it, the triangle would be squashed flat.

config.successText: Every sin and cos value sits below $1$, which is exactly why the other two sides always come out shorter than the hypotenuse. Keep that as the sanity check for the next slide.

altExplain.prompt: Name the sides first: $x$ is across from $35°$, so it is the opposite, and $12$ is the hypotenuse. Opposite and hypotenuse is sin, and multiplying both sides by $12$ frees $x$.

interaction.hint: Name the two sides in play, pick the ratio that pairs them, then rearrange.

config.intro: Same frame as Pythagoras: build the working line by line, and the mark codes show what each line earns.
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='91.2,259 388.8,259 91.2,49' fill='rgba(240,238,234,0.05)' stroke='#c8c6be' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><path d='M 104.2 259 L 104.2 246 L 91.2 246' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><path d='M 388.8 259 L 364.8 259 L 364.8 257.8 L 364.9 256.5 L 365.1 255.3 L 365.3 254.1 L 365.6 252.9 L 365.9 251.7 L 366.3 250.6 L 366.8 249.4 L 367.3 248.3 L 367.9 247.2 L 368.5 246.2 L 369.2 245.2 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='354.8' y='247' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>35°</text><text x='75.2' y='154' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='end' dominant-baseline='middle'>x</text><text x='253.8' y='134.4' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff4670' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>12 cm</text></svg>

options.whyWrong: Cos pairs the adjacent with the hypotenuse, but $x$ is across from the angle, the opposite.
The hypotenuse goes on the bottom of the sin ratio, and $12$ is the hypotenuse here.

lines.label: the value of $x$
lines.nudge: Multiply both sides by $12$, then type $12 \times \sin(35)$ into the calculator: it gives $6.883...$, which rounds to $6.88$.

config.successText: $x = 6.88$ cm, shorter than the hypotenuse as it must be. Ratio line for the method mark, value for the accuracy mark.

slides.title: When the unknown is on the bottom

altExplain.prompt: The known side touches $52°$, so it is the adjacent, and the unknown is the hypotenuse: that is cos. When the unknown sits on the bottom of the fraction, the rearrangement is a division: $h = 9.5 \div \cos 52°$.

interaction.hint: The unknown is the hypotenuse this time, so it lands on the bottom of the ratio, and the rearrangement becomes a division.

config.prompt: Find the hypotenuse $h$ to $1$ decimal place.
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='158,259 322,259 158,49' fill='rgba(240,238,234,0.05)' stroke='#c8c6be' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><path d='M 171 259 L 171 246 L 158 246' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><path d='M 322 259 L 298 259 L 298.1 257.2 L 298.3 255.4 L 298.6 253.6 L 299.1 251.8 L 299.7 250.1 L 300.5 248.5 L 301.3 246.9 L 302.3 245.3 L 303.4 243.9 L 304.6 242.5 L 305.9 241.3 L 307.3 240.1 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='288' y='247' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>52°</text><text x='240' y='281' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#00abfa' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>9.5 m</text><text x='258.9' y='139.2' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>h</text></svg>

options.whyWrong: The hypotenuse always sits on the bottom of the cos ratio, and here the hypotenuse is $h$.
Sin pairs the opposite with the hypotenuse, but $9.5$ m touches the angle, so it is the adjacent.

lines.label: the value of $h$
lines.nudge: Rearranging gives $h = 9.5 \div \cos 52°$. The calculator gives $15.43...$, which rounds to $15.4$.

config.successText: $h = 15.4$ m, and it is the longest side, which is the instant sanity check. Unknown on the bottom always means dividing.

interaction.hint: The ratio line and the final value are judged separately, and a length can never be negative.

config.prompt: This candidate's calculator was set to the wrong mode. Rule on each mark.
config.question: Find $x$: the side opposite $35°$, with a hypotenuse of $12$ cm.

judgments.label: the ratio line
judgments.explain: The ratio is named and arranged correctly, so the method mark is safe.
judgments.whyWrong: Line 1 pairs the opposite with the hypotenuse under sin, which is exactly right.

judgments.label: the final value
judgments.explain: A side of $-5.14$ cm is impossible: the calculator was in radians, where $\sin 35$ means something different. In degrees the answer is $6.88$.
judgments.whyWrong: Look at the sign of the answer. Can a length be negative?

config.faultExplain: The working was right and the calculator was wrong. A negative or absurd value is the radians giveaway: switch the mode to degrees and redo the last line.
config.successText: One mark kept, one lost to a settings menu. Checking the degrees symbol on screen takes two seconds and has saved thousands of marks.

visual.content:
chapter 4 of 5
Finding an angle

Two sides are known and the angle is missing. The inverse buttons turn a ratio back into an angle.

Still 2 marks: the ratio line earns the method mark even before the inverse is applied. Angle answers go to 1 decimal place.

interaction.hint: The question asks WHICH angle has a sin of $0.5$. There is a button that answers exactly that.

options.whyWrong: $60°$ is the angle whose COS is $0.5$. Sin and cos swap roles between the two acute angles.
The ratio is not the angle. The $\sin^{-1}$ button converts the ratio $0.5$ back into the angle that made it.

config.successText: $\sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30°$. Each ratio has its own inverse button, and turning a fraction of sides back into an angle is the whole job of this chapter.

altExplain.prompt: The two known sides are the opposite ($7$) and the hypotenuse ($12$), which is sin. Write $\sin\theta = 7/12$ first, then apply $\sin^{-1}$ to the fraction.

interaction.hint: Name the two known sides, write the ratio, then apply the matching inverse button.

config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='93.8,259 386.3,259 93.8,49' fill='rgba(240,238,234,0.05)' stroke='#c8c6be' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><path d='M 106.8 259 L 106.8 246 L 93.8 246' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><path d='M 386.3 259 L 362.3 259 L 362.3 257.8 L 362.4 256.5 L 362.5 255.3 L 362.8 254.1 L 363.1 252.8 L 363.4 251.6 L 363.8 250.5 L 364.3 249.3 L 364.8 248.2 L 365.4 247.1 L 366.1 246 L 366.8 245 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='352.3' y='247' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>θ</text><text x='77.8' y='154' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff822c' text-anchor='end' dominant-baseline='middle'>7 cm</text><text x='254' y='134.5' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff4670' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>12 cm</text></svg>

options.whyWrong: Tan is opposite over adjacent, and the $12$ cm side faces the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse.

lines.label: the angle
lines.nudge: $\sin^{-1}(7 \div 12)$ on the calculator gives $35.68...$, which rounds to $35.7$.

config.successText: $\theta = 35.7°$. The ratio line alone earned the method mark, exactly as the mark scheme promises.

slides.title: Now with the two shorter sides

altExplain.prompt: Neither known side is the hypotenuse: $8$ is across from $\theta$ and $5$ touches it. Opposite over adjacent is tan, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(8/5)$.

interaction.hint: Check whether the hypotenuse is even involved before choosing the ratio.

config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='174.4,259 305.6,259 174.4,49' fill='rgba(240,238,234,0.05)' stroke='#c8c6be' stroke-width='2.2' stroke-linejoin='round'/><path d='M 187.4 259 L 187.4 246 L 174.4 246' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><path d='M 305.6 259 L 281.6 259 L 281.7 257 L 282 255 L 282.4 253 L 283 251.1 L 283.7 249.2 L 284.6 247.4 L 285.7 245.6 L 286.9 244 L 288.2 242.5 L 289.7 241.1 L 291.2 239.8 L 292.9 238.6 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><text x='271.6' y='247' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>θ</text><text x='240' y='281' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#00abfa' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>5 m</text><text x='158.4' y='154' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff822c' text-anchor='end' dominant-baseline='middle'>8 m</text></svg>

options.whyWrong: Sin needs the hypotenuse on the bottom, and neither of these sides is the hypotenuse. A sin above $1$ is also impossible.
That is the tan of the OTHER angle. The opposite of $\theta$ is $8$, and it goes on top.

config.successText: $\theta = 58.0°$. Two legs and no hypotenuse always means tan. Remember these numbers: they return in the next chapter.

visual.content:
chapter 5 of 5
The exam

The exam dresses these questions in words: angles of elevation, ladders, masts. Find the triangle, then it is the same two lines.

A real past-paper elevation question first, then two full solves with no help.

interaction.hint: Elevation starts from flat. Imagine looking straight ahead first, then tilting your eyes up.

config.prompt: Stand at the blue point and look at the top of the wall. The angle of elevation is measured between which two lines?

options.text: The wall and the line of sight
options.whyWrong: That is the angle at the top of the triangle, the depression seen from up there, not the elevation from the ground.

options.text: The flat horizontal and the line of sight

options.whyWrong: That is just the right angle where the wall meets the ground. It is always $90°$ and never the answer.

config.successText: Elevation is measured up from the horizontal to your line of sight. The height and the horizontal distance are then opposite and adjacent, which is why elevation questions are nearly always tan.

slides.title: Real exam question · Cambridge s24_21 Q7(b)(i)

altExplain.prompt: Two marked distances along the ground differ: the horizontal gap is $21 - 16 = 5$ m, and that first subtraction earns its own mark. Then the height $8$ is opposite the angle and the $5$ is adjacent, which is tan.

interaction.hint: The first mark is for finding the horizontal distance hiding in the two ground measurements.

config.prompt: A face of a prism is $8$ m tall. A point on the ground is $21$ m from a wall that stands $16$ m before it. Find the angle of elevation of the top from that point.
config.contextHtml: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 320' preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' style='display:block;width:100%;height:100%' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><line x1='40' y1='276' x2='440' y2='276' stroke='#7a7875' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='356' y1='276' x2='356' y2='102' stroke='#7a7875' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='96' y1='276' x2='376' y2='276' stroke='transparent' stroke-width='1'/><line x1='96' y1='276' x2='356' y2='116' stroke='#ff4670' stroke-width='2.2'/><path d='M 96 276 L 130 276 L 130 274.4 L 129.9 272.9 L 129.7 271.3 L 129.4 269.8 L 129.1 268.3 L 128.7 266.7 L 128.3 265.2 L 127.7 263.8 L 127.1 262.3 L 126.5 260.9 L 125.7 259.5 L 125 258.2 Z' fill='rgba(255,240,103,0.18)' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.2'/><circle cx='96' cy='276' r='4.5' fill='#00abfa'/><path d='M 343 276 L 343 263 L 356 263' fill='none' stroke='#fff067' stroke-width='1.6' opacity='0.9'/><text x='148' y='264' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='15' font-weight='600' fill='#fff067' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>θ</text><text x='226' y='296' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#00abfa' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='middle'>21 − 16 = 5 m</text><text x='372' y='196' font-family='Geist Mono,monospace' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#ff822c' text-anchor='start' dominant-baseline='middle'>8 m</text></svg>

lines.label: the horizontal distance
lines.nudge: The point is $21$ m out and the base sits $16$ m along, so the gap between them is the difference.

options.whyWrong: The slanted line of sight is the hypotenuse and its length is unknown, so sin has nothing to work with. A sin above $1$ is impossible anyway.
The height $8$ is across from the angle of elevation, so it goes on top.

lines.label: the angle
lines.nudge: The same $\tan^{-1}(8 \div 5)$ as the last chapter: $58.0°$.

config.successText: $58.0°$, and the same triangle you solved a moment ago was hiding inside a prism question the whole time. The subtraction earned a mark on its own.

config.successText: $\theta = 38.2°$. Name the sides, write the ratio, press the inverse: the whole topic in three moves.

slides.title: You banked 15 marks of examiner working
slides.prompt: Every mark used the same opening move: name the sides against the marked angle, then write the ratio. That line alone earns the method mark on plain triangles, on hypotenuse rearrangements, and inside a real prism question.

slides.prompt: Pythagoras for two sides, trig for a side and an angle, and the naming step before everything.
bullets: Name the sides against the marked angle before choosing anything.
SOH CAH TOA picks the ratio; the ratio line with numbers in earns the method mark.
Unknown on the bottom of the fraction means dividing, not multiplying.
Inverse buttons turn a ratio back into an angle, to $1$ decimal place.
Elevation questions are tan questions: height over horizontal distance.
